How Queen of the Night can work in a room: color, scale and framing

November 26, 2026 · Kimberly Marnell Art

A painting can give a room a point of attention without matching every fabric or object around it. Queen of the Night by Kimberly Marnell combines a dark-haired figure, closed eyes and a large white flower with soft washes and expressive botanical marks. Start with whether you want to look at that image every day, then check how it will sit in your space.

The original is watercolor, acrylic marker and ink on paper, listed at 24 × 18 inches and sold unframed. Its portrait composition suits a vertical space. The product page shows the current availability, price, close-ups and other views; use those alongside the measurements when deciding.

Choose the role you want the painting to play

In a reading corner, the inward-looking figure could become a quiet point of focus near an armchair. In a bedroom, the soft washes could sit alongside restrained textiles. In a living space with more pattern, the strong dark hair and distinct face could provide a recognizable visual anchor.

These are styling possibilities, not photographs of a client’s installation or a promise that the work will fit every room. A large, busy wall may make an unframed sheet feel smaller than you expect. A narrower wall, an intimate grouping or a position viewed from nearby may let the details hold attention.

Use one or two colors as a connection

The painting includes blush pink, pale green, white, dark hair, warm skin tones and brighter botanical accents. Try connecting one or two of those notes to something already in the room: a soft green textile, a warm wood surface or a dark lamp. You do not need to introduce every color.

For a calm setting, give the painting some plain wall around it and let a few surrounding materials repeat its warmth. For a more expressive setting, compare the scale of nearby patterns so they do not obscure the face and flower. View the artwork image in the room’s daytime and evening light; screen colors cannot establish an exact match to a physical wall or fabric.

Make a paper template before choosing its position

  1. Mark out a 24 × 18 inch rectangle in the painting’s portrait orientation. Use paper or low-tack tape appropriate for your wall finish; test tape in a discreet spot first.
  2. Stand where you normally enter or sit in the room. Check the rectangle’s relationship to the furniture and nearby art.
  3. Allow additional space for a mat and frame. The listed dimensions describe the artwork, not a finished framed installation.
  4. Once a framer has confirmed the proposed outside dimensions, repeat the template at that full size before buying hanging hardware.

A room-view image is useful for imagining placement, but your measurements and the chosen frame should govern the final decision. A digital image alone cannot confirm scale on your particular wall.

Plan the frame for an original work on paper

A slim dark frame could connect to the figure’s hair and lines. A light wood frame could connect to warm furnishings. These are options to compare with the actual painting, not included framing choices.

Tell your framer the medium and that this is an original on paper. Ask about suitable conservation mounting, a spacer or mat to keep the work away from glazing, and glazing options for the location. Check the actual sheet and desired edge visibility before ordering a frame solely from the nominal size. Framing is additional to the unframed artwork price.

Choose a dry indoor position away from strong direct sunlight and splashes. Review reflections from nearby windows or lamps before deciding on a hanging position.

Original painting or a small printable reproduction?

If you want the one-of-a-kind paper original, review Queen of the Night’s photos, current availability and purchase details. The listing includes free US shipping and a signed certificate of authenticity. Read the linked returns policy and check delivery questions before ordering.

If your space or plans call for a small printable reproduction, Queen of the Night is also included in the Figurative Art Trio as a bordered 5 × 7 inch print. That download is a different product: it is not the original, and printing, paper and a frame are your responsibility. For larger reproductions or other materials, check the fine art print options rather than enlarging the small printable file.

For a specific framing or delivery question about the original, ask Kimberly about Queen of the Night. Include the question and any relevant wall dimensions. No room photo is necessary to browse or purchase the listed work.
